protocol: A 37-year-old pilot was exposed in a decompression chamber. The paragraph introducing the case calls it in-flight, while the numbered case explicitly describes simulated altitude in a chamber.
outcome_window: Symptoms during the chamber run, immediate improvement on descent and intermittent residual symptoms over the next 24 hours.
note: Fryer investigated this case and presents it in the respiratory syndrome section. Selection-programme membership and the at-risk exposure denominator are unavailable.

protocol: An aircrew officer was deliberately exposed in a decompression chamber. Similar episodes on at least five earlier flights are historical context for this one chamber episode.
outcome_window: During the chamber run and subsequent gradual fading of the skin changes over several days.
note: The selected narrative provides neither a date nor an exposure denominator. Earlier flight episodes lack individual profiles and are not separate case rows.

protocol: A 29-year-old navigator reached 37,000 ft and played cards at altitude. He was transferred to the chamber lock because of limb pain.
outcome_window: The source follows limb pain at altitude, a post-descent visual disturbance and headache, and resolution of all symptoms.
note: The author describes the delayed syndrome as migraine-like. The navigator reported a similar antecedent episode of visual disturbance and headache without a medical diagnosis. The selected chamber episode has no exposure denominator.

protocol: A 25-year-old cadet was exposed to 28,000 ft and transferred to the lock for rapid descent.
outcome_window: During exposure and descent, through recovery and the author's interview a few days later.
note: The reported difficulty initiating voluntary movements was clarified in a later interview. A specific diagnosis of diplegia was unsupported. Membership in the 28,000-ft RAF selection cohort is unresolved. The Navy in-flight comparison is a different case.

protocol: A 28-year-old pilot with prior reported flight bends was exposed in a decompression chamber. The paragraph introducing Cases 21 and 22 dates the two RAF hospital admissions to 1960.
outcome_window: During exposure and descent, through immediate hospital recovery and repeat plasma volume testing.
note: This is one of two cases selected for plasma-volume assessment in the same report. The RAF selection-programme crosswalk and an exposure denominator are unavailable. The author describes the repeat difference as within normal variation.

protocol: A 31-year-old pilot was exposed in a decompression chamber. The paragraph introducing Cases 21 and 22 dates the two RAF hospital admissions to 1960.
outcome_window: During the chamber run, post-descent assessment and repeat plasma volume testing one week later.
note: The original report discusses dye mixing and other limitations when interpreting the low initial plasma volume. Programme overlap and an at-risk denominator are unavailable.

protocol: A 30-year-old medical officer accompanied a pilot as an observer during a routine chamber exposure. His own symptoms are the subject of the case.
outcome_window: Hip and buttock pain at altitude resolved on descent. Later recurrent hyperventilation attacks were observed in the respiratory laboratory.
note: Fryer describes post-descent paroxysmal hyperventilation following pain he interpreted as bends. The later episodes supply differential-diagnosis evidence. Neither the pilot's outcome nor an exposure denominator is available.
